Thanks to FLT#941 every definition in FLT now has a docstring :-) I got Claude to find them all and write docstrings (on my $20 account I ran out of credits so had to wait 4 hours and then tell it to start again, but it finished in the second period) and then I read them all manually (they were super-easy to find now because they were in the github diff) and modified a fair few in a final commit. I think the main time-saver was simply not actually having to find the declarations manually.

FWIW here was the prompt. I ran it with --dangerously-skip-permissions in a sandbox (which Claude also wrote for me, which was the main reason I ran out of credits in the middle).

You're in the FLT project. Right now scripts/nolints.json contains a ton of lines
each of which silence a linter because a declaration doesn't have a docstring.
Can you populate the branch kbuzzard-add-docstrings with commits which create a
docstring for each of the declarations with no docstring? Just have a go at the
docstrings. If you want to know what a Lean docstring looks like then I can
recommend looking in .lake/packages/mathlib which contains a copy of Lean's
maths library, which is full of docstrings. After you've made all the
docstrings, delete all the lines in scripts/nolints.json and see if the repo
still lints. You can run lake lint to lint the repo. For example, right now
lake lint should pass, but if you delete a random line in
scripts/nolints.json then it should fail and the failure will tell you exactly
where in the repo the docstring needs to be added.

Here is a strategy which might work. Switch to main. Delete a line from
nolints.json. Run lake lint. Find where the docstring needs to go. Then put
the line back in nolints.json. Now switch to kbuzzard-add-docstrings. Add
the docstring. Now go back to nolints.json and delete the next one. Continue
until all docstrings are added. Or do something smarter than this. Note that if
you edit a lean file in the repo and then run lake lint then it might
recompile everything. This is why I suggest you make edits on the branch but
only ever lint on main.

For a docstring please try and give something descriptive. If you don't have a
clue, just write "this is claude -- I don't know a good docstring" or whatever.
I will manually review all docstrings after so don't worry, you can get some
wrong. I know the codebase well. Good luck! You can do it! Please ask if you
need any help.

By the way, you're in a sandbox which might not be set up correctly. If you try
to do something and you can't then please feel free to complain.

Good luck! You can do it! Please ask if you need any help.
